checks.name: exact_target_preserved

evidence.reason: No-controller branch uses time.Duration(rand.Int63())%minVal and r.clock.After; with the default realClock this equals the original randomTimeout + time.After.
Installs conf.Random and conf.Clock, then substitutes realClock{} when Clock is nil, so production wiring is unchanged by default.
Aux goroutines run the identical closure bodies that were previously launched with plain go; only their shutdown joinability is added.
Nil-default Random and Clock fields are additive and preserve existing production configuration behavior.

checks.reason: All core-file changes are default-disabled hooks. When no controller is configured, Raft.random is nil, Raft.clock falls back to realClock (delegating to time.Now/time.After), waitWhilePaused is an atomic-load early-out, and auxGo wraps the same function bodies that were previously plain goroutines. The original package-level randomTimeout remains intact and is only referenced from util_test.go now, while the no-controller path in randomTimeoutFor is byte-for-byte the original algorithm.

checks.name: message_cache_injection_coherence

evidence.reason: Struct backed by unexported uint64, stable while pending and never reused.
Underlying string with ten request/response kind constants matching the transport families.
Required fields Handle, Source, Target, Kind, Message appear in order; the extra Stream field is typed, documented, and only non-nil for InstallSnapshot.
Plain sentinel errors ErrMessageNotPending, ErrTargetUnavailable, ErrMessageNotAccepted are errors.Is-classifiable.
Controlled mode deep-copies the payload and captures before waitRPC; the base transport send is not invoked, so the original send is suppressed.
Resolves owner.base.peers[addr], enqueues the controller private copy into peer.consumerCh, removes on confirmed acceptance, and preserves the entry on closed-owner/unavailable/timeout.
Returns copyPayload + copyBytes fresh snapshots, so Pending views never alias the private copy that Inject delivers.
removeLocked uses an order-preserving slice splice, so Drop/Clear/Inject never reorder surviving entries.

checks.reason: The controller-owned seam is a real Transport wrapper installed before NewRaft, so every in-boundary AppendEntries/RequestVote/RequestPreVote/InstallSnapshot/TimeoutNow/pipeline request is captured before any delivery; responses are captured as separate pending entries with reversed routing and fresh handles. The cache is a mutex-guarded ordered slice plus map, Pending returns fresh deep copies, handles are monotonic and invalidated on Drop/Clear/Inject, Inject resolves the real target via the owning base transport peers map and enqueues into the target consumer channel (the same ingress InmemTransport.makeRPC uses), and acceptance removes the entry while failures preserve it. Concurrent Inject is serialized by an injecting flag for single delivery.

checks.name: original_send_suppressed

evidence.reason: if !t.controlled() delegates to t.base; otherwise it captures and waits, never invoking t.base.AppendEntries/makeRPC.
Controlled mode returns a controlledPipeline whose AppendEntries captures instead of opening an inmemPipeline on the base transport.
The only write to peer.consumerCh in controlled mode; the RPC carries a fresh RespChan that feeds awaitResponse rather than the base transport's makeRPC.

checks.reason: In controlled mode every outbound transport method captures into the controller and returns without calling the wrapped InmemTransport's send path; the base transport's consumer channel is then written only by MessageController.Inject. Disabled mode delegates directly to the base, keeping production behavior intact.

checks.name: protocol_logic_unchanged

evidence.reason: waitWhilePaused returns true immediately while paused is false, so FSM application proceeds exactly as before by default.
Added stopCh/shutdownCh cases only abort when the transfer is already being abandoned; normal replication signaling is unchanged.
Pause gate and clock routing are default-inert; the original replication/backoff/heartbeat logic is preserved.
Original function remains in production code for util_test.go compatibility and defines the unchanged algorithm/domain.

checks.reason: The core hooks are inert by default. The pause gate is a single atomic-load check before each loop select; randomTimeoutFor falls back to the global rand source and realClock; the leadership-transfer abort cases are only reachable when stopCh or shutdownCh is closed, which never happens during normal protocol operation. Default Config.Clock nil keeps time.After/time.Now behavior, so state transitions, persistence, ordering, and timer arming are unchanged.

checks.name: testing_contract_conformance

evidence.reason: Exported constructor with variadic *Raft; Pause/Resume/Stop/Crash/Restart take ServerID and return error; ErrLifecycleUnsupported is errors.Is-classifiable.
Per-owner deterministic controller; Choices returns deep-copied []RandomChoice with Name/Owner(ServerID)/Value(time.Duration).
NewTimeController(unit, nodes...) -> TimeController with Clock() and Advance(steps) error; Config.Clock installed pre-NewRaft.
Exported thread-safe controller; NewControlledTransport wraps an InmemTransport as a LoopbackTransport installed before NewRaft.

checks.reason: All fixed surfaces required by the common contract are exported production APIs with concrete target-native types: MessageController/Pending/Drop/Clear/Inject and three classifiable errors; LifecycleController with Pause/Resume/Stop/Crash/Restart and ErrLifecycleUnsupported; RandomController/RandomChoice/Choices with ServerID owner and time.Duration value; TimeController/Clock/Advance with a positive-step shared virtual clock. Constructors, wiring fields, and usage paths are reachable from an external consumer and installed before goroutines start.

risks: Concurrent Drop or Clear during an already-in-flight Inject is not serialized against delivery: the injecting flag guards Inject-vs-Inject, but Drop/Clear remove the entry without checking injecting, so a message whose delivery has begun can still be enqueued after it was concurrently removed. This does not corrupt cache state or reorder entries, but the 'remove without delivering' guarantee is best-effort under that specific race.

The awaitResponse goroutine launched after a request is accepted can linger if the target node stops/crashes without responding while the source transport remains open; it only exits on the source transport close. This has no protocol impact and only affects controller bookkeeping.

Pause acknowledgment is sent by any gated loop (main, replication, FSM, snapshot), so Pause's quiescence guarantee is best-effort: work already in flight can still complete at the pause boundary, as documented.

Wall-clock timeouts remain in ControlledTransport.waitRPC, the controlled pipeline, and Inject's enqueue; these are RPC delivery deadlines, not protocol timers, and are disclosed as outside the time-control scope.

TimeController.Register is bookkeeping-only and is not automatically re-bound by LifecycleController.Restart (Advance is clock-driven and the fresh runtime inherits Config.Clock); a re-register after restart returns a duplicate-ID error.
